'''Complex convexity''' is a general term in [[complex geometry]].

== Definition ==
A set <math>\Omega</math> in <math>\Complex^n</math> is called {{nowrap|<math>\Complex</math>-convex}} if its intersection with any complex line is contractible.<ref>{{citation
 | last1 = Andersson | first1 = Mats
 | last2 = Passare | first2 = Mikael
 | last3 = Sigurdsson | first3 = Ragnar
 | doi = 10.1007/978-3-0348-7871-5

 }}.</ref><ref>{{cite journal |jstor=24493584|title=An Example of a Bounded C-Convex Domain Which is Not Biholomorphic to a Convex Domain|last1=Nikolov|first1=Nikolai|last2=Pflug|first2=Peter|last3=Zwonek|first3=Włodzimierz|journal=Mathematica Scandinavica|year=2008|volume=102|issue=1|pages=149–155|doi=10.7146/math.scand.a-15056|doi-access=free|url=https://ruj.uj.edu.pl/xmlui/handle/item/85869}}</ref>

== Background ==
In [[complex geometry]] and [[complex analysis|analysis]], the notion of [[convex function|convexity]] and its generalizations play an important role in understanding [[function (mathematics)|function]] behavior. Examples of classes of functions with a rich structure are, in addition to the convex functions, the [[subharmonic function]]s and the [[plurisubharmonic function]]s.

Geometrically, these classes of functions correspond to convex domains and pseudoconvex domains, but there are also other types of domains, for instance lineally convex domains which can be generalized using [[convex analysis]].

A great deal is already known about these domains, but there remain some fascinating, unsolved problems. This theme is mainly theoretical, but there are computational aspects of the domains studied, and these computational aspects are certainly worthy of further study.
